newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says West Bank "political" murder disturbing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says West Bank "political" murder disturbing.

text.p: The United States said on Monday it would consider it "highly disturbing" if a Palestinian man killed last week in the West Bank died for political reasons.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the administration would withhold judgment until completion of a police investigation.
But he said "if this turns out to have been what is now alleged -- a political murder -- that will be highly disturbing, obviously, to the United States."
Farid Bashiti, 70, was found dead in PLO-ruled Ramallah in the West Bank on Friday amid accusations he sold land to Jews.
Security sources said he was discovered bound and with signs of a blow to the head by a sharp object. Israel was investigating the death after Palestinian security forces handed over the body.
The fatality occurred after the Palestinian Authority said last week it would apply the death sentence to Palestinians who sold land to Israelis.
Burns, asked if the United States believed Palestinians should be free to sell their land to whomever they want, called it a "loaded question."

"I think obviously we hope that people are, both the Israelis and Palestinians, free to conduct business affairs within the law, as the law established, and when the law is absolutely clear and accepted by both sides," he said.

U.S. Middle East Coordinator Dennis Ross is in the region trying to help Israel and the Palestinians resume peace talks which broke off in March when Israel's Likud government broke ground for new Jewish settlements in East Jerusalem.
Burns said Washington preferred "to use our influence privately ... rather than to put ourselves into a position where we become one of the actors in these controversies."

"But at this point, there's been a murder. No evidence and no suspects. It's very difficult for the United States to leap ahead with you and to confirm everything that's appearing in the newspapers. We have to be responsible about what we say," he said.
